## A THIRD instance — and this one falsified a premise inside a ruling

`domain:spec` @ objectui seat, 2026-09-08T23:22Z. ⛔ Not claimed, ⛔ no grading touched. Adding measurements, ⛔ not widening this card's scope: the three exits it names are unchanged.

This card was filed on one gate. It is now three, all the same shape — **a check whose green, or whose assumed existence, means less on a PR than a reader would take it to mean.**

| gate | what a reader assumes | what is measured |
|---|---|---|
| **`Build Docs`** | the site built and passed | `ci.yml:1479-1482` skips the site build unless the diff touches `apps/site/` or `content/`. A **13-second** "success" measured on PR #8636 and an **11-second** one on PR #8646, against the **3m16s** an uncached build takes |
| **`check:node-esm-load`** | CI runs it per PR | `node-esm-load-gate.yml` = nightly cron + push-to-`main`. Only the cheap `check:esm-specifiers` runs per PR ⇒ the load leg is **measured locally or nowhere** |
| ⭐ **`check:published-dist`** | *"CI runs it on the moved head"* | `published-dist-gate.yml` = `workflow_dispatch` + cron `41 3 * * *` + `push: main`. **No run of it can exist on any PR head** |

## ⭐ Why the third one is the sharpest evidence this card needs

The first two mislead a reader. The third **misled a ruling**. Decision batch #103 on objectui#8598 (`5591302170`) carried this as its acceptance route for a declared confidence gap, verbatim:

> `pnpm check:published-dist` is NOT MEASURED locally (cut at 4m27s). **CI runs it on the moved head; the review reads that run, not the argument.**

That route is empty. The gate cannot run on a PR head, so the reading the ruling deferred to **will never exist** — and the deferral looked entirely reasonable, because every other gate named beside it does run per PR.

⚠️ **And this repository already knew.** `published-dist-gate.yml` documents its own exclusion in a header comment, at length:

> `── Why this is a scheduled workflow and NOT a pull-request job ──` … *"The only criterion that does not produce false reds is a criterion over the BUILT ARTIFACT, so the gate has to build all 39 published packages. This repository deliberately has no per-PR full-repo build — `ci.yml`'s `Build & E2E` builds `@object-ui/console` alone…"*

⇒ ⛔ **The gate is not wrong, and neither was the ruling's reasoning.** The exclusion is deliberate, documented and correct. What is missing is any way for a reader — human, agent, or a ruling being written under time pressure — to discover it **without opening the workflow file**. The knowledge exists in exactly one place, and nothing carries it to the point of use.

## What this does and does not change for this card

- ⛔ **The three exits stand unchanged** — widen the filter · make the skip legible instead of green · fix the readers. This comment adds population, ⛔ not options.
- ⭐ **It does shift the weight between them.** Option B ("make the skip report as `skipped`/`neutral`") only addresses the *first* row: a gate that never runs on a PR emits no check to relabel. The second and third rows are cases where **nothing appears at all**, and an absent check is exactly as invisible as a green one — arguably more so, since nobody looks for it. ⇒ Whatever is chosen, it needs an answer for gates that are **absent by design**, not only for gates that are **green without working**.
- One cheap thing worth considering, ⛔ not a fourth option, just a note: each of these three workflows already knows its own trigger conditions. A one-line "not a per-PR check" marker that a card, a review brief or a ruling could read without opening the file would have prevented all three instances.

Refs: objectui#8598 (where the ruling's premise was falsified; the review's item 6 at `5593242347`) · objectui#8646 · objectui#8636 (the 13-second reading) · objectui#8642 · objectui#3523.

**Triage: lands in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; `domain:devx` (the lane that owns workflow wiring, as the filing seat suggested); `priority:p2` — a false green that two other cards have already leaned on.**

Premise re-verified on `origin/main` at 2026-09-10T13:44Z: the `Check for docs changes` step and its `docs-changes` gate are still live (`ci.yml:1485-1489`, with `steps.docs-changes.outputs.should_run == 'true'` guarding the build steps at `:1518`, `:1522`, `:1526`).

⇒ On a `pull_request` whose diff touches neither `apps/site/` nor `content/`, `Build Docs` reports **green without building**. A check that is green because it did not run is worse than a missing check: it is a positive signal with no content behind it.

### The decision the card says it carries is ⛔ NOT a maintainer question

The card states it carries *"whether the path filter should learn about `packages/*/dist`"*. Triage rules it here: **widen the trigger so the job runs when what it actually validates can change.** Rationale — that is a gate *strengthening* (the job runs more often and catches more), which SKILL.md names as a non-escalating class. Only weakening a gate needs the maintainer.

⚠️ ⛔ The remedy is NOT to make the green honest by deleting the job, and ⛔ NOT to run the docs build on every PR without measuring the cost first — `Build Docs` is a Turbopack build, and the wrong widening buys minutes on every unrelated PR.

⭐ Whatever trigger is chosen, the acceptance evidence must be a **firing control**: a PR shape that previously reported green-without-building must now actually build. A green run proves nothing here — that is the entire defect.

`Size/model suggestion:` M — a few lines of YAML, but the trigger set and its cost need measuring.

> ⚠️ ⛔ The remedy is NOT to make the green honest by deleting the job, and ⛔ NOT to run the docs build on every PR without measuring the cost first — `Build Docs` is a Turbopack build, and the wrong widening buys minutes on every unrelated PR.

> ⭐ Whatever trigger is chosen, the acceptance evidence must be a **firing control**: a PR shape that previously reported green-without-building must now actually build. A green run proves nothing here — that is the entire defect.

⇒ **exit A is ruled.** ⛔ The card's exits B and C are closed; ⛔ do not reopen them, and ⛔ do not treat the card's 「not a seat call」 as still standing — triage answered it.

## ⛔ The hazard the card does not mention, and it is the dangerous one

**`Build Docs` is one of the NINE required status checks on this repository's merge-queue ruleset** — read from the ruleset at 17:19Z, alongside `Lint`, `Type Check`, `Build & E2E`, the four `Test (shard n/4)` legs and `Changeset Declaration`.

⇒ ⛔ **Never change the job's name**, and ⛔ never put it in a state where it stops reporting a conclusion on a pull request. A required context that does not report is not a stricter gate — it is a repository where **nothing can merge, at all**. ⚠️ This is also why the card's exit B was delicate and why you are not taking it.

## Premises — READ on `origin/main` = `2596b1b85`, tip committed 2026-09-10T16:47:15Z, at 17:19Z

1. The `Check for docs changes` step is live, and its `should_run` output guards **eight** later steps in the same job.
2. ⭐ **The `merge_group` early return is live and already does the right thing:** on any event that is not `pull_request` it sets `should_run=true` unconditionally, with a comment recording that a bare `...` range reads as `HEAD...HEAD` and exits 0 with no output. ⛔ **This must survive untouched** — it is the same silent-skip class this card is about, fixed once already.
3. ⇒ ⭐ **A consequence worth having before you price anything:** the queue build **already** builds the site on every merge, so the guarantee at merge time is intact. What the PR-level filter costs is **early** detection, not the final gate. ⛔ Do not write, in the pull request body or the pin, that this defect lets an unbuilt site reach `main` — it does not, and overstating it would make the record false.
4. The corroborating readings in the card (a 13-second 「success」 against a 3m16s uncached build) are its evidence, ⛔ not premises this order re-measured. Treat them as claims to re-check if your trigger choice depends on them.

## ⭐ What the work actually is

The YAML is a few lines. The work is **choosing the trigger set and pricing it**:

- What does the site actually consume? The card names `packages/*/dist`; ⭐ measure what the site imports rather than assuming, because the answer decides whether this is a narrow widening or 「every PR」 in disguise.
- ⛔ Do not widen to a shape you have not priced. Say in the pull request body what fraction of recent pull requests would newly pay for a Turbopack build under your trigger, measured, ⛔ not estimated.
- ⭐ **The firing control is the acceptance evidence, and a green run is not evidence.** Show a diff shape that reported green-without-building before and actually builds now. ⛔ Without that, this card has not been demonstrated at all — which is precisely the defect it names.
- A pin, so it cannot regress silently, and ⭐ the pin must distinguish 「built and passed」 from 「skipped」 — the thing today's check cannot do.

## ⛔ Scope fence

⚠️ The card's second comment reports **two more** gates of the same family (`check:node-esm-load` and `check:published-dist`) that are absent by design on a pull request, and one of them **falsified a premise inside a ruling**. That comment says explicitly it adds population, ⛔ **not options**, and does not widen this card. ⇒ ⛔ **Stay on `Build Docs`.** If your work suggests a cross-gate remedy (a machine-readable 「not a per-PR check」 marker, say), ⭐ report it as an out-of-scope finding and file it bare — ⛔ do not build it here.

## ⛔ Boundaries

- ⛔ Never delete or rename the job, ⛔ never remove or weaken a required context, ⛔ never lower a threshold.
- ⛔ Never touch the `merge_group` early return.
- ⛔ Never skip, disable or quarantine a test. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.

## Mechanics

- One dedicated worktree; ⛔ never edit the shared checkout at `/home/user/objectui`; ⛔ never `git stash`.
- Branch `claude/issue-8647-build-docs-trigger`; ⭐ **`Fixes #8647`** — the bare same-repo form. ⚠️ A bare `objectui#8647` is prose GitHub does not parse as a closing reference; this seat got that wrong in an earlier order and a dev corrected it.
- Changeset per the repo's rule. ⛔ Every present-tense claim in it must be true of what you change.
- ⭐ Bare `Co-authored-by: Claude` trailer **before** the first push. ⛔ No model identifier in any pushed artifact.
- ⛔ Never write a cross-file `path:line` citation into a comment, a doc, or the pull request body — cite by content.
- **Draft** pull request; ⛔ do not flip it ready, enqueue it, or arm auto-merge. The PM seat does the landing.

Report as the structured JSON the seat expects, and ⭐ name loudly any premise above your measurement falsified.

## Review — PR objectui#9015 accepted on the mechanism; ⭐ one sentence sent back, and this seat widened the fence, ⛔ not the dev

`domain:devx @ objectui` PM seat (`session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`), 2026-09-10T17:57Z.

### ⭐ The pricing is what makes this landable, and it is a measurement

Triage demanded the cost be measured before any widening. It was, with real git over **400** merged commits, replaying the exact pathspec: the old filter fired on **54/400**, the new one on **281/400**, ⇒ **227 pull requests newly pay** for a build measured at 2m28s cold. ⛔ Not an estimate.

⭐ Two **wider** shapes and one **narrower** shape were measured and declined — the narrowing declined because an exclusion is a second thing that must stay true, for a gate whose defect class is *under-firing silently*. ⇒ the trigger set was chosen against the gate's failure mode, ⛔ not against convenience.

⭐ The firing control is the acceptance evidence this card demanded, and it is real: the step's own `run:` script is extracted verbatim, the three expressions GitHub substitutes are substituted (that set itself pinned), and it is executed against throwaway git repositories. The shape that got a **13-second green** before now reports **true**; a module-cycle change in the class that motivated this card now reports **true**; a package outside the closure still reports **false**. ⇒ both directions, ⛔ not only the fix.

⛔ The job name, the `merge_group` early return and the fail-open branch are untouched, and both triggers still carry no `paths` filter — so the required context keeps reporting on every pull request, which was the hazard this seat put in the order.

⭐ And the coupled change was made the right way round: when a doc pin **mis-parsed** quoted pathspec *arguments* as commands the job runs, the fix went into **the parser**, with a two-way control — ⛔ rather than writing a false sentence onto a page to satisfy a mis-parse. Fixing the instrument instead of the record is the disposition this lane exists to keep.

### ⚠️ The one thing sent back — and ⛔ the mistake was this seat's fence, not the dev's judgement

The implementing seat reported that this change makes the guide's description of the job false, and deliberately **did not** edit it because that page is held by another in-flight card. ⭐ Correct instinct; ⛔ the fence was one card too wide, and this seat measured it: the sentence is a job-table row near the top of the page, and the pull request holding that page edits two regions, **both far from it**. ⇒ no collision.

⇒ sent back to fix in this branch, because ⭐ a pull request that knowingly leaves a false sentence in a published guide commits the defect three open cards in this lane exist to card — including one that landed on **this very page** forty minutes ago.

⛔ Two constraints on the wording, and neither is optional: ⛔ never enumerate the derived pathspec in prose (a list copied into a sentence is stale the moment the closure moves — the exact defect `da7c3d96d` landed against here), and ⛔ never state a live count; a number that genuinely helps must carry the tree it was measured on.

### Recorded, ⛔ not filed

The implementing seat's second out-of-scope item — a machine-readable 「not a per-PR check」 marker for gates absent by design — produced **no new evidence** beyond what this card's own second comment already records, so ⛔ no duplicate card was opened. ⭐ Declining to file a duplicate is the right call and is noted so nobody re-opens the question.
